title: Transport of the cocartesian criterion from essential-image tests
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent Hom bifunctors, mapping-composition homotopies and whole-square pullback invariance from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality], [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] and [lem-coef-kan-nerve-pullback-recognition]. Let $p:E\to B$ and $q:F\to B$ be inner fibrations of small quasicategories, let $T:E\to F$ be a functor equivalence with $qT=p$, and fix an edge $e$ of $E$. If the cocartesian criterion square for $T(e)$ is a homotopy pullback at every test vertex $Tz$ with $z\in E$, then it is a homotopy pullback at every vertex $w\in F$. The comparison for $w$ is obtained from an equivalence $Tz\to w$ and its image in $B$, with the coherent composition and inverse homotopies retained.

source.place: Essential-image test-object transport in the mapping-square marking argument extracted from Proposition 2.4.4.3 (dual), after the image-test comparison and before applying the cocartesian mapping criterion.

proof.text: Because $T$ is a functor equivalence in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], choose a quasi-inverse $S:F\to E$ and a coherent natural equivalence $\eta:TS\to\mathrm{id}_F$, an equivalence edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(F,F)$ with inverse edge $\eta'$ and the two inverse-triangle $2$-simplices. Fix a vertex $w\in F$ and put $z=S(w)$. Evaluation at $w$ is a simplicial map $\operatorname{Fun}(F,F)\to F$; it sends $\eta,\eta'$ and the two $2$-simplices to an edge $u:Tz\to w$, an edge $u':w\to Tz$ and $2$-simplices with boundary triples $(u,u',\mathrm{id}_{Tz})$ and $(u',u,\mathrm{id}_w)$, so $u$ is an equivalence edge of $F$. Applying the simplicial map $q$ to these data makes $q(u)$ an equivalence edge of $B$, and $qT=p$ gives $q(Tz)=p(z)$. The edge $u$ and its inverse data are retained for step 3.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3 (dual), essential-surjectivity step; the definition of a functor equivalence and its coherent inverse triangles.

proof.text: Write $e:x\to y$, $a=T(x)$, $b=T(y)$ and $s=T(e):a\to b$; then $q(s)=p(e)$ by $qT=p$. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ with $F,B$ $\mathcal U$-small, so that their mapping spaces are $\mathcal U$-small. The Hom-bifunctor node [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality], applied to $q:F\to B$, gives coherent Hom bifunctors $H_F,H_B$ and a coherent natural transformation $q_*:H_F\to H_B\circ(q^{\mathrm{op}}\times q)$, that is, a simplicial map $\Delta^1\times F^{\mathrm{op}}\times F\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$. Precompose it with $\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1}\times s^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathrm{id}_F$, where $s^{\mathrm{op}}:\Delta^1\to F^{\mathrm{op}}$ is the edge $s$ read in $F^{\mathrm{op}}$ from $b$ to $a$. By the definition $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathscr C)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(K\times\Delta^n,\mathscr C)$ this is the same as a simplicial map $\Phi:F\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1\times\Delta^1,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$, with $\Phi(\sigma)$ the composite of $\mathrm{id}\times\sigma$ with that map for each simplex $\sigma:\Delta^n\to F$. For a vertex $v$, $\Phi(v)$ is the coherent square with corners $H_F(b,v)$, $H_F(a,v)$, $H_B(qb,qv)$, $H_B(qa,qv)$, whose horizontal edges are the first-variable actions of $s$ and $q(s)$ and whose vertical edges are the components of $q_*$, with the naturality simplices of $q_*$ as its commutation datum. By the Hom-bifunctor node these values are the right-pinched spaces $\operatorname{Map}_F(b,v)$, $\operatorname{Map}_F(a,v)$, $\operatorname{Map}_B(q(b),q(v))$, $\operatorname{Map}_B(q(a),q(v))$, the first-variable actions are precomposition with $s$ and $q(s)$ in the canonical composition classes of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], and the components of $q_*$ are the maps applying $q$ to simplices. Thus $\Phi(v)$ is a coherent square presenting the criterion square of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] for the inner fibration $q$, the edge $s=T(e)$ and the test vertex $v$, with the commutation datum supplied by the coherent naturality of $q_*$ and not only by the four corners.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3 (dual), mapping-square criterion and functoriality of the Hom bifunctor in the test variable.

proof.text: The simplicial map $\Phi$ carries $u$, $u'$ and the two inverse-triangle $2$-simplices of step 1 to an edge $\Phi(u):\Phi(Tz)\to\Phi(w)$, an edge back and $2$-simplices witnessing that they are inverse; so $\Phi(u)$ is an equivalence edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1\times\Delta^1,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})=\operatorname{Fun}(N([1]\times[1]),\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$, an equivalence of whole coherent square diagrams. On corners it is postcomposition with $u$ in $F$ and with $q(u)$ in $B$, and its higher simplices are the composition and naturality homotopies of the Hom bifunctors. The whole-square invariance clause of [lem-coef-kan-nerve-pullback-recognition] therefore gives: $\Phi(Tz)$ is cartesian if and only if $\Phi(w)$ is cartesian.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3 (dual), transport along an equivalence of test objects.

proof.text: For each vertex $v$ of $F$, the clause of [lem-coef-kan-nerve-pullback-recognition] on an equivalence between a coherent square and a strict or specified homotopy-commuting presentation, applied to the presentation of step 2, says that $\Phi(v)$ is cartesian if and only if the canonical map from $\operatorname{Map}_F(b,v)$ to the path-space fiber product $\operatorname{Map}_F(a,v)\times_{D,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,D}\operatorname{Map}_B(q(b),q(v))$ with $D=\operatorname{Map}_B(q(a),q(v))$, built with the given commutation datum, is a weak homotopy equivalence. This is exactly the meaning of homotopy pullback in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. By hypothesis this holds for $v=Tz$, so $\Phi(Tz)$ is cartesian. By step 3 $\Phi(w)$ is cartesian, so the criterion square for $T(e)$ at $w$ is a homotopy pullback. Since $w$ was arbitrary, this is the conclusion. When $w=Tz'$ already, nothing needs proving; when $e$ is degenerate the same argument applies unchanged; when $F$ has no vertices the conclusion is vacuous.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3 (dual), essential-image transport of the mapping-square cocartesian criterion; source read online and not archived locally.

(3) Φ(u) is an equivalence of whole squares, so whole-square invariance applies. (4) The recognition theorem's presentation clause matches the criterion node's path-space definition of homotopy pullback, so the property moves from Tz to w. proof_deps are the same 5 nodes and split_report.summary was updated.
